simple.meaning: תָּכָה (tâkâh) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to strew , i.e. encamp.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Deuteronomy, beginning at Deuteronomy 33:3. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to תָּכָה (H8497) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: תָּכָה (tâkâh) / H8497 is traced through Deuteronomy 33:3 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H8497. takah [ תָּכָה ] verb meaning wholly dubious; — Pu`al Perfect 3plural לְרַגְלֶ֑ךָ תֻּכּוּ וְהֵם Deut 33:3 ; were led or assembled would suit context; see especially Dr Berthol. תְּכוּנָה see כון
